dedupe_keys.name: united states economy wide impacts of h5n1 avian influenza in dairy cattle

description: This case study uses a computable general equilibrium (CGE) model to simulate the short- to medium-term economic impact of the highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 outbreak in US dairy cattle on gross domestic product, the dairy sector and the main trading partners. The authors, researchers at Imperial College London, the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, the Center for Global Development, Umeå University and the University of Oxford, published it in an open-access journal article. Scenarios cover the current situation and realistic and reasonable worst cases. Coverage is the US and its main trading partners. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence. Caveats: scenario inputs are uncertain because the outbreak was still evolving, and CGE models smooth over short-term market frictions. The study estimated domestic losses of 0.06 to 0.9 percent of US GDP and dairy sector losses of 3.4 to 20.6 percent, with trading partners increasing dairy output to compensate; current government subsidies cover about 1.2 percent of output losses, likely too little to motivate farmers to step up surveillance and biosecurity. Simulation uses: shock scenarios for food supply chain resilience and for linking animal health events to wider economic models. Related records: the African swine fever study (case_study-us-african-swine-fever-outbreak-economy-wide-cge) applies a similar model to the pork sector, and the GTAP Data Base (data-gtap-data-base) supplies global trade data of the kind CGE models use.
